decisive_question.question: Is the sharp de-rate a temporary overshoot around a lowered 2026 guide and a contained On-X recall — with On-X/stent-graft/tissue growth and NEXUS restoring the EBITDA trajectory — or the start of an earned, terminal re-rate as recall, leverage and negative LTM FCF impair the franchise?

evidence_for.claim: Constant-currency revenue grew 12% and adjusted EBITDA ~26% in Q1 2026, with On-X +17%, stent grafts +10% and tissue processing +23% — the core growth mechanism remained intact through the drawdown.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Artivion, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 07, 2026.rtf

evidence_for.claim: NEXUS FDA approval plus the exercised Endospan option is a dated, mechanism-bearing catalyst that management frames as completing a market-leading aortic-arch portfolio.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ Key Developments: Artivion Inc NYSE AORT Key Developments.rtf · Apr-07-2026

evidence_against.claim: Management LOWERED full-year 2026 earnings guidance on May-07-2026, the direct trigger of the gap-down and the anchor for the ~82% GAAP-EPS consensus cut.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ Key Developments: Artivion Inc NYSE AORT Key Developments.rtf · May-07-2026

evidence_against.claim: The May-23-2026 On-X voluntary recall directly threatens the highest-growth franchise, while 3.7x total-debt/EBITDA leverage and negative LTM FCF (-$7.3M) leave little cushion.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ Key Developments: Artivion Inc NYSE AORT Key Developments.rtf · May-23-2026

key_unknowns: Scope, cost and duration of the On-X voluntary recall (May-23-2026) and whether it impairs the 17%-growth valve franchise — no quantified financial impact is disclosed in the facts.

Company-adjusted LTM EBITDA and adjusted forward EV/EBITDA are UNKNOWN (not in the revised 99.1 guidance), so leverage on the company's own adjusted basis and a clean forward multiple cannot be verified.
No segment-level EBITDA is disclosed (only revenue split Products 78% / Preservation Services 22%), an opaque profitability gap — a bearish disclosure gap.

Whether FY2026 revised guidance ($480–496M revenue; $100–107M adjusted EBITDA) fully embeds the recall and lowered outlook, or leaves further downside — the revised-guidance block itself parsed as UNKNOWN.

Covenant headroom: financial-maintenance covenants referenced (min interest coverage, max leverage) are from stale/older facilities; the governing terms for the 2031 secured loans are not confirmed against current 3.3x–3.7x leverage.
Reconciliation of the transcript-stated net leverage 1.8x vs the CIQ-computed net-debt/EBITDA 3.3x — the bases differ (company-adjusted vs GAAP LTM) and the true covenant basis is unresolved.
Timing and terms of the Endospan close and its incremental debt/dilution, given financing is 'in place' but the full-cost and share impact are not quantified in the facts.
Data vintage: export date is unverified (a floor ≥ 2026-06-30) and TEV as-of (2026-06-25) is vintage-incoherent with multiple pricing (2026-06-30), flagged for a re-pull.

caveats: P/E may be distorted by non-recurring EPS — latest annual EPS 0.21 vs recent median -0.54; verify against normalized/forward EPS (CIQ)

Net debt/EBITDA (3.3x) is on REPORTED EBITDA (CIQ / consolidated GAAP), not the covenant basis; management and credit covenants typically define leverage on adjusted EBITDA (a larger denominator → a lower ratio), reconciled in the earnings release/transcript (currently UNAVAILABLE) — do not read 3.3x as the covenant-basis leverage.

Distorted-P/E anchor (a bull point): 'EV/EBITDA (TEV/LTM) sits at 20.6x, ~7th percentile of its own 42-quarter range (median 32.1x), a near-floor own-history reading that poses the overshoot question.' — the P/E is distorted (rests on a non-current/non-recurring EPS); don't read it as cheap

business_description.value: Artivion, Inc. manufactures, processes, and distributes medical devices and implantable human tissues worldwide. The company offers On-X prosthetic aortic and mitral heart valves; On-X ascending aortic prosthesis; CarbonAid CO2 diffusion catheters; Chord-X ePTFE sutures; pyrolytic carbon coating services; E-vita Open NEO, a hybrid stent graft; Arcevo, an LSA hybrid stent graft system; AMDS hybrid prosthesis; and NEXUS ONE, an endovascular stent graft system. It also provides NEXUS DUO, an aortic arch system; NEXUS TRE, a custom-made three branch graft; E-vita thoracic 3G, a stent graft system; E-xtra Design Engineering, a range of stent graft systems for the treatment of aortic vascular diseases, such as TAAA and Artivex; E-nside, a multibranch stent graft system; E-tegra, an AAA stent graft system; E-ventus BX and Tuva BX balloon-expandable peripheral stent grafts; and E-liac, a stent graft used to treat aneurysmal iliac arteries. In addition, the company offers synthetic vascular grafts that are used in open aortic and peripheral vascular surgical procedures; BioGlue, a surgical sealant; CryoValve SG pulmonary heart valve; CryoPatch SG pulmonary cardiac patch; SynerGraft, a decellularization technology; vascular preservation services; and PhotoFix, a bovine pericardial patch fixated. It markets its products and preservation services primarily to physicians through a direct sales team to hospitals and other healthcare facilities. The company was formerly known as CryoLife, Inc. and changed its name to Artivion, Inc. in January 2022. Artivion, Inc. was incorporated in 1984 and is headquartered in Kennesaw, Georgia.
